title: Cyber Defenders Unit 1 · Messages on the move (3-5)

choices: A small numbered piece of a message
A very big envelope for one photo
A road between two houses
A lock that seals a message

items.q: Why does every packet carry a number?
choices: So routers can charge for each road
So the far end can rebuild the message in order
So the message travels much faster
So anyone can read it easily

items.q: Why does a private message need protection on its journey?
choices: It does not, because packets are too small to read
Because numbers hide the words inside each packet
Because every hand that carries a packet could peek
Because routers always lose the first packet

items.q: Which symbol shows a connection is sealed?
choices: A postcard picture
A padlock
A road sign
An open envelope

items.q: Sam is about to send something private on an open network. What is that network like?
choices: A sealed envelope
A locked box
A postcard anyone can read
A private letter

items.q: What does the padlock NOT promise?
choices: That the sender is kind and honest
That the trip is sealed
That others cannot peek on the trip
That the envelope stays closed on the way
A soft place in the sky that holds photos
A kind of rain that carries messages
Someone else's big computers that keep copies safe
A folder that only exists on your tablet

items.q: Why can a sent photo not be unsent?
choices: Copies can be forwarded, and you cannot call them back
Photos always vanish after one day
Friends never share copies with others
The cloud deletes every copy at once

items.q: Which picture passes the noticeboard test?
choices: A private secret about a friend
A sunny drawing you would happily pin up in town
A photo your friend asked you to keep private
A shiny secret you found by accident
